name: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, Last Prince of Wales
summary: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, recognized by the Treaty of Montgomery (1267) as Prince of Wales with authority over all other Welsh lords, is killed in a minor skirmish at Orewin Bridge in December 1282, apparently not recognizing the ambush until it was too late. His death immediately collapses Welsh resistance; his brother Dafydd is captured and executed in 1283. Edward I completes the conquest.

_quarry.structural_significance: Llywelyn's death transforms Wales from an autonomous principality into an English-administered territory; the execution of the male Gwynedd line eliminates potential future centers of resistance; the cultural significance is enormous, the Welsh bards commemorate Llywelyn's death as the end of Welsh political sovereignty that would not be restored until the 20th-century devolution; the Statute of Rhuddlan (1284) imposes English legal and administrative structures
